minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved a new seasonal cemetery laborer job at grade 5, with high school diploma only preferred.
minutes.summary: The committee approved prior minutes, noted a school IT employee moved to the town as network administrator, and spent most of the meeting on a new seasonal cemetery laborer job description. After debate over grade 4, 5 or 6 against the union laborer rate, members settled on grade 5 and changed the diploma requirement to preferred. The meeting then adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee placed a new seasonal cemetery laborer job at grade 5 on the Salary Administration Plan.
The committee dropped the strict high school diploma requirement; the posting will say diploma or equivalent preferred.
Members compared grades 4, 5 and 6 against the union laborer rate and seasonal wages in nearby towns before settling on grade 5.
The vote on the amended job description was taken by roll call, but the captions do not make the result clear.
A school IT employee moved to the town as network administrator, placed at a step matching his school salary; the form goes out by DocuSign.

why_it_matters: The grade sets the hourly pay for two seasonal cemetery positions that town meeting already funded, so it bears on what the cemetery budget has to cover.
Dropping the diploma requirement widens who can apply for the seasonal cemetery jobs.
watch_next: The roll-call result on the amended job description is not clear in the captions; check the town's official minutes for the recorded vote.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the substance: the Grade 5 seasonal cemetery job description with a diploma-or-equivalent-preferred adjustment, the Network Administrator PAF going out for electronic approval, and the attendees. The main difference is the dollar figures (the 33.11 network administrator rate, the 18.24 seasonal rate and the grade ranges), which only our minutes carry and the captions garble.
